classification.difficultyReason: Students fill in a supplied two-way outcome table: colour probabilities from two bags of different sizes, then the four independent joint products. Part b adds two cells. Part c uses the complement (1 − P(BB)) or three cells. Mostly routine independent-event work with a table as scaffold, so it sits below the without-replacement tree question.

content.prompt:
Bag 1 contains 2 red (R) and 3 blue (B) counters.
Bag 2 contains 5 red (R) and 3 blue (B) counters.
One counter is picked from each bag.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Complete the table by writing the probability of each colour for each bag and the probability of each pair of outcomes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the probability of picking counters of different colours.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the probability of picking at least one red counter.

answer.worked:
The complementary event is two blue counters.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one R})&=1-P(BB)\\&=1-\frac{9}{40}\\&=\frac{31}{40}\end{align*}$$
